beur-hagra/1:א: (1) One may not knead. Rashi wrote the reason: because in the rainy season the sun travels in the lower parts of the sky and the springs boil, as written 94b. And R' Eliyahu Mizrachi wrote the reason: because at night the sun travels below the ground — see there; and their words appear from our words that by day springs are cold and at night they boil. And Rif explained what is written at the end of chapter Kol Sha'ah: the drawn water that was drawn on that day — and it is implied from his words that drawing from the attached source heats them and requires overnight standing; therefore he calls them drawn water because drawing heats them — see R' Eliyahu Mizrachi. According to Rashi, whatever stood 12 hours detached, even from morning until evening, is sufficient; and according to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi, specifically when it was not attached at night; and according to his words, even after the beginning of the night it is permitted to knead with them provided it was not attached at the beginning of the night. But R' Yehuda bar Natan wrote, and likewise Semak in the name of R' Yitzchak and Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 5, that the end of the night causes cooling because the north wind blows from midnight onward until dawn, as written at the beginning of Berachot; and it is cold, as written in Bava Batra 25b: from adulterers comes this north wind; therefore one must leave them the entire night — and so Rashba that one must leave them the entire night.
beur-hagra/1:ב: Between, etc. For Rashi, specifically cistern and spring water; but in rivers there is no concern, for specifically springs boil, as written in the Gemara: springs boil — and the reason is they are close to their exit from the source; and likewise according to R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's explanation. And Rashi wrote: nevertheless one should not breach the fence of the early authorities; but according to Rif's explanation it is forbidden by law.
beur-hagra/1:ג: While it is still day, etc. For R' Eliyahu Mizrachi wrote that according to R' Eliezer of Metz one must draw them specifically at bein ha shemashot so they remain attached all day, for by day springs are cold as written — and so Semak; and some are stringent to draw between day and night; and some forbid when drawn while it is still day even if left overnight afterward. Semak there rejected this because he mentioned only overnight standing — implying one need not be concerned when they were drawn, only that they stood overnight; and Beit Yosef rejected R' Eliyahu Mizrachi's words and explained "while it is still day or bein ha shemashot" means only that one should not draw after the beginning of the night; but Beit Yosef was concerned for the stringent view and wrote close to bein ha shemashot and not while it is still day. However, from the conclusion of all poskim and from the language of the Gemara it is implied like Shulchan Aruch's view; and likewise from Rif's language that he wrote they were drawn on that day.
beur-hagra/1:ד: And one may not knead, etc. To be concerned for R' Yehuda bar Natan's view as above.
beur-hagra/1:ה: Possibly. All of the above interpretations:
beur-hagra/1:ו: And if the weather. To cool them specifically according to Rif's explanation, that the reason they became warm when drawn and need cooling.
beur-hagra/1:ז: We need to be. In the end of the day, there is nothing to drink:
beur-hagra/1:ח: And even. As written end of chapter 3 of Yoma: a cloudy day is entirely sun — for Rava's exposition: a woman should not knead, etc.
beur-hagra/1:ט: And if not. As Rambam and Shulchan Aruch siman 259 seif 8 wrote — see what is written there.
beur-hagra/1:י: And when carrying, etc. See Magen Avraham:
beur-hagra/1:כ: When it falls. For Shabbos does not prepare for Yom Tov, as written at the beginning of Yom Tov; and he follows his reasoning that he ruled one must draw them specifically at bein ha shemashot or close to it — see Magen Avraham.
beur-hagra/1:ל: L'chatchila, etc. As above, springs boil — which is not so with rivers:
beur-hagra/1:מ: But when the rivers. As written there that the sun travels in Nissan in the mountains in order to thaw the snows and they become lukewarm:
beur-hagra/1:נ: One may not pour out. As written "a keeper of a mitzvah knows no evil" — and Taz.
beur-hagra/1:ס: And also forbidden. For it is a preparer of mitzvah; and see above siman 464 as written:
beur-hagra/1:ע: And even. Lest one put chametz into it:
beur-hagra/1:פ: And it is customary to take. As written in Maggid Mishneh regarding Chanukah — and specifically in earthenware; see siman 453 seif 3.
beur-hagra/2:א: Seif 2: some say water. See Magen Avraham.
beur-hagra/2:ב: And one should not be lenient. For they nevertheless heat from their connection to the ground — see Beit Yosef:
beur-hagra/3:א: Seif 3: one may not knead. Pesachim 42a — and they are equal that there is no, etc.
beur-hagra/3:ד: Whether with water. According to Rif's explanation, drawn water means water not left overnight, and the question also refers to water not left overnight.
beur-hagra/3:ה: And there are those who disagree. According to Rashi who explains drawn water means from a kettle, etc., as above — thus the question does not apply at all to water not left overnight:
beur-hagra/3:ו: And some say that b'shogeg, etc. For one transgressed intentionally as written chapter 2 of Yoma 17: they asked — if one transgressed and baked, etc.; and there it deals with intentional as written 99b, etc.; provided he does not deceive, etc.; this case of deception is different, etc.; 99b: one who cooks, etc.; and the first reasoning holds we also find one transgressed b'shogeg, as written chapter 3 of Shabbos: they asked — if one transgressed and stayed, what? And according to Rif's explanation there they asked regarding metsamek ve-yafeh whether it is forbidden b'shogeg — see Tosafot there; and proof from the pastries of Eretz Yisrael; and we are not concerned for such a case; but Rashi and Rosh rejected there and said because it is close to intentional; and all the more so for those who baked in our presence — see R' Eliyahu Mizrachi siman 226.
beur-hagra/3:ז: And even without, etc. Since there are those who permit even intentionally, as above:
beur-hagra/4:_: Seif 4: water not, etc. And some say one in two, rather in majority as Semag and Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote; and the reason: since the majority is cold it cools — as Tosafot wrote Shabbos 42a s.v. noten; rather it appears as Rabbenu Tam says, etc.
beur-hagra/5:_: Seif 5: it is customary, etc. And even. They bring proof to forbid from what is written chapter 8 of Shabbos and in Gittin: matzah that is not salted; and in Chullin they said salted is like boiling and is like kneading in hot water — as above seif 3; and chapter 4 of Shabbos; and not regarding salt that adds vapor; and chapter 2 of Bava Batra: they distance salt because of heat — as written in the Gemara there. And this is what Baer Heitev wrote: and even b'dieved, etc.; and so Mordechai; and as above seif 3. But many poskim permit and reject their proofs: that which "not salted" means it lacks preparation like "not sharpened"; and that which "salted is like boiling" — they state explicitly only when it is not eaten because of its salt — see Yoreh De'ah siman 98 and siman 105; and likewise that of Shabbos and Bava Batra where there is much salt; and Rashba siman 224 that it is not like boiling but to absorb and extract, etc.; but to heat, etc. And Ran brings proof to permit from end of chapter Kol Sha'ah from what is written: and soaked in water and salt is forbidden — implying specifically when cooking it heats; but for bread, no — and so Rashba, except he wrote people are accustomed to be stringent.
beur-hagra/6:א: Seif 6: since it has. In the Gemara there they say specifically that he added flour to it; and Tosafot wrote this sugya argues on that of Zevachim where they said even though the majority is rice, etc. — majority of Torah law; and we rule like the sugya of Zevachim that taste in a kezayit in a place of Torah law obligates, as Tosafot wrote; and likewise Tur explained in Yoreh De'ah; and this is what Shulchan Aruch wrote: since, etc.
beur-hagra/6:ב: Nevertheless. The Ra'avad in chapter 12 of Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot forbids in cooked dishes that become chametz; and what is written in Menachot "seasoned," etc., and so in Tosefta and Yerushalmi chapter Kol Sha'ah — matzah seasoned is discussed when seasoning is after baking; but in Yerushalmi chapter 2 halachah 4 it is not so, for R' Simon in the name of R' Yehuda bar Levi said: that kezayit with which a person fulfills on the 15th of Nissan must not have liquid come into it, etc.; and it was taught: one fulfills with seasoned matzah even though it has no taste of grain — they thought to say seasoned means liquids; it was said seasoned means spiced; nuts — therefore permitted even before baking, for after baking rich matzah is not relevant; and as written siman 462 seif 4; and so Ra'avad in laws of matzah chapter 6 because of rich matzah it is forbidden.
beur-hagra/6:ג: And pepper. For it is not called spice as Tosafot wrote chapter 1 of Yoma in the name of Tosefta; and pepper is likewise as spice — see Tosafot Pesachim 105a s.v. atei, etc.; and it heats as written in Niddah: she ate pepper and saw — see there in Shulchan Aruch siman 129.
beur-hagra/6:ד: And likewise. As written chapter 3 of Shabbos and chapter 2 of Bava Batra.
chok-yaakov/1:א: Or at bein ha shemashot. The main time to draw is between sunset and nightfall before the moon shines on the ground — so too Maharil; see above siman 261 for the measure of bein ha shemashot. Since not everyone knows how to measure bein ha shemashot, one draws close to bein ha shemashot after sunset. B'dieved, if drawn while it is still day or drawn after the beginning of the night, it appears from the later authorities one may be lenient to knead with them after 12 hours. In responsum of Magen Avraham siman 32 he wrote one should not be lenient unless in a time of pressure or great loss — see above seif 3. See Taz who wrote it is better after drawing than before. However Maharil wrote the opposite — end quote: it is better to draw a little early than to delay, for overnight standing is not mentioned explicitly in the Talmud — end quote; his words appear correct and so implies Magen Avraham.
chok-yaakov/1:ב: Under the ceiling. And that he did not mention to cover with a cloth as written below — because they must be in an exposed place where air rules, as the Mechaber wrote in the name of Or Zarua; if one covers with cloth they become warm. According to this it is not correct that people are careful to cover water specifically even in cold weather; we must say therefore covering at night is ineffective because we are concerned he might forget to bring them in for a long time by day and they will heat via the cloth or covering if not covered well — unlike below when carrying water only via transit, any covering helps:
chok-yaakov/1:ג: And when carrying water under the open sky. This refers to the above that he wrote it is good to place them under the ceiling so that if he forgets to bring them in at dawn the sun will not shine on them. Therefore he also wrote: be careful also when carrying water by day under the open sky to the kneading house to cover it with a cloth so they will not become warm, as Semag and Semak wrote and Terumat HaDeshen siman 115 explicitly; and so Levush explained it deals by day — in the evening hour when they draw, since the sun already set, one need not cover them at all; it is only custom and extra caution lest something heating fall in, as Terumat HaDeshen wrote there. All this is simple and clear, unlike Magen Avraham who explained it refers to the time of drawing.
chok-yaakov/1:ד: One must cover them. Specifically in earthenware or wood vessel and the like — covering helps; but if they are in a glass vessel, covering does not help, for since the sun shines through glass it heats more than if exposed — as in chapter 2 of Beitza daf 33a — see Rashi there and above siman 472; requires study:
chok-yaakov/1:ה: Eve of the 13th, meaning Thursday night. For on Thursday night one is concerned lest he draw before Friday sunset or delay and violate Shabbos — so is the language of Mordechai end of the first chapter of Pesachim; from this it is implied b'dieved if he forgot to draw on the night of the 13th he may draw on Friday while it is still day close to bein ha shemashot or even at bein ha shemashot, for we are not concerned for Shabbos violation, for anything that is due to shevut they did not decree against at bein ha shemashot in a place of mitzvah, as explained above siman 261 and Shaarei Teshuvah there. However from Rokeach siman 265 and as brought by later authorities who wrote: when the 14th falls on Shabbos they draw on the night of the 13th from the river or well and do not draw from the cistern in his courtyard on Shabbos for kneading because he needs much and it appears like filling his garden and ruin as in Eruvin 104 — end quote — it appears that even b'dieved drawing is forbidden; and in truth Rokeach's words seem astonishing, for what prohibition is there, since it appears like filling — for there it is explained specifically via a wheel it is forbidden because he draws much and draws easily; and even with our wheel some permit as explained above siman 338 seif 16 — all the more so what they draw now for an individual in his house one or two buckets, which is a small matter, and also at bein ha shemashot where they did not decree shevut. If so, what prohibition is there? Rokeach's words can be answered with difficulty that his intent is if he wants to draw on Shabbos itself, as somewhat implied in his language, and not at bein ha shemashot; and it deals when they want to draw much for the courtyard — but not when forgotten for an individual, permitted to draw one or two buckets in his courtyard at bein ha shemashot or even in the river where carrying is permitted (however from later authorities who brought Rokeach it does not imply so). More plausible is concern for preparing from Shabbos to Yom Tov: (found in Shaarei Teshuvah siman 7 permission via small vessels and many people for this reason does not help). This concern is also in Beit Yosef and Magen Avraham, and they conclude one who forgot to draw on the night of the 5th should draw on Friday while it is still day, or command a gentile at bein ha shemashot, or take water drawn in his house even if not drawn for the mitzvah since impossible otherwise — end quote; and it is better to draw oneself or via agent that day close to bein ha shemashot where there is no prohibition concern like other ways — see above s.k. 1 and responsum of Magen Avraham siman 32 who wrote: the custom spread not to knead matzah after Shabbos except with water drawn on the eve of the 6th, for one can limit drawing at bein ha shemashot unlike two bein ha shemashot of Erev Shabbos; and what he wrote: where there is custom one should not be lenient unless pressure or great loss — end quote; nevertheless where there is no custom one should not be stringent and should not act as he wrote.
chok-yaakov/1:ו: To draw from wells. Maharil wrote: it is a good custom first to clean and purify the spring; and if impossible to clean all of it because of many water sources, nevertheless draw much water from it before drawing. And all cisterns in houses — generally much water was drawn in them to clean vessels for Pesach days — end quote; and in Shaarei Knesset HaGedolah: our custom is to filter water through a white cloth so nothing falls in — end quote. All this is only stringency l'chatchila — see above siman 457 s.k. 12 and siman 467 seif 12.
chok-yaakov/1:ז: Nevertheless l'chatchila it is good to place iron in them. Take new iron and hang it on a rope — Maharil and later authorities. Magen Avraham wrote in Darkei Moshe in the name of Hagahot Maimoniyot: on all other days of the year one places salt or a seal — end quote. Taz wrote: nevertheless it appears that on other nights if he did not place iron to guard from tekufah he may discard them if he can easily be without those waters, unlike these waters of matzah of the mitzvah where it is forbidden to discard, for it appears contemptuous of the verse "He who keeps a mitzvah knows no evil" — end quote; and similarly Maharshal in his explanation to Semag; and the rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek objected that his words imply only matzah of the mitzvah permits keeping the water, but even for other matzot one need not be particular about tekufah if one died; nevertheless he concludes in the name of Agudah that even for matzah of the mitzvah one permits only when impossible to borrow mayim shelanu in that city. It appears simple that even Agudah who is stringent speaks only in a small city with few people, but in a large city one is certainly not obligated to go door to door for water, only among neighbors and acquaintances — and so implies Taz's language that even all year one should not be stringent if he cannot easily be without that water — all the more so these waters; and the custom is to be lenient in every regard.
chok-yaakov/1:ח: Also forbidden for a gentile to draw. That is l'chatchila; and so explicit in Maharil that it is extra stringency l'chatchila; and so Shlah.
chok-yaakov/1:ט: And it is customary to take designated water. One says at the time of drawing for the sake of the mitzvah of matzah — Maharil and Mahariv siman 193; and Maharil wrote further that some take designated water each night independently.
chok-yaakov/1:י: New earthenware vessels, etc. In all books of Shulchan Aruch it is written thus in the name of Kol Bo, but I did not find it in his words. Magen Avraham wrote: Mateh Moshe wrote one should not take a vessel that had fruit juice, for fruit juice with water hastens to become chametz. (It appears to me through boiling it is permitted.) Also one should not take a copper vessel that heats — end quote; however I have seen practice kneading in copper troughs — end Magen Avraham. In truth one can distinguish: mayim shelanu require cooling, and in copper perhaps they do not cool — unlike for kneading; see gloss in minhagim forbidding drawing in copper too — so practice; b'dieved do not forbid — and so Ateret Zekenim siman 459; and so appears from what is written seif 3 on thick copper rim.
chok-yaakov/2:א: Cistern. This is what Talmud calls a pit — water collected in a building in the ground separated from the ground and covered above, as if drawn; not comparable to ar'ar kastin covered above — do not draw close to drawing because constantly flows from river; but if leaving overnight like other water, permitted to draw under pipe or ar'ar like river or well or kastin itself if covered.
chok-yaakov/2:ב: Unless in a time of pressure. If he has drawn mayim shelanu in his house he should take them even if there is concern they were drawn by day or at night; see Beit Yosef and R' Eliyahu Mizrachi and Bach siman 7; see what is written above s.k. 1 and s.k. 5 in the name of Magen Avraham.
chok-yaakov/3:א: One may not knead in hot water. Levush wrote: even if left overnight all night and heated only by the sun — thus his intent: even mayim shelanu, as long as they are still hot, it is forbidden to knead with them; unlike if they are cold before us, for which overnight water is needed to remove heat from the sun, as explained in the Talmud and poskim; and the same for copper-kettle water if cooled, as poskim and Mechaber imply who wrote "and water inside is lukewarm" — specifically while still lukewarm. However in responsum of Rama siman 35 he wrote: copper-kettle water, even after cooling, should be forbidden, for an intentional transgressor — not to mention R' Eliezer of Metz, for even water not left overnight, cooling does not help — all the more so hot water; and even per Rashi in copper-kettle water there is no remedy; therefore we do not find any posek who wrote there is remedy for copper-kettle water — end quote. In truth the Mechaber's implication is not so — see Ateret Zekenim; and so the rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek from Mahari Weil; the poskim did not need to write remedy because copper-kettle water is stated, and whatever cooled is no longer copper-kettle water; and since they are cold before us, what prohibition is there — and on the contrary I have heard that sometimes water that was boiled and cooled is colder than other water. What he wrote that for R' Eliezer of Metz cooling does not help for water not left overnight is not necessary — see Beit Yosef. Although Mahari Weil that the brother-in-law brought concludes: heaven forbid to contradict their words without proof — it appears he understood Levush's "even if left overnight" means even if cooled; therefore he did not come to contradict his words. In truth Levush's intent is simple as written; and proof is clear from Talmud and poskim and Mechaber who wrote specifically hot or lukewarm; one who wants to be stringent in any case has permission to permit b'dieved.
chok-yaakov/3:ב: That its copper is thick. Magen Avraham wrote: the same applies to earthenware.
chok-yaakov/3:ג: Lukewarm. That is, like warmth of saliva; Yerushalmi chapter Kol Sha'ah halachah 7: although in Menachot kneaded lukewarm and they guard lest they become chametz because priests are zealous — in matzah even priests should not knead lukewarm lest distinguish matzah from matzah — end quote; see Menachot 55a; explained in Tur and Beit Yosef: in benefit permitted for all even kneading in hot water.
chok-yaakov/3:ד: If it is on the roof and on. A little last is getting worse at it and you don’t move from the rabbi’s stop and VAT I won’t take them out by a plighting duty for the first nights to see the column:
chok-yaakov/4:_: One in two. It implies specifically one in two; see Sefer Me'irat Einayim general rule 91 s.k. 6; see Magen Avraham; and it is implied from poskim brought in Beit Yosef that if mixed during kneading it is not nullified — we require specifically mixed before kneading. The rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek raised b'dieved to permit even in such a case — see above s.k. 16; Magen Avraham wrote permitted to mix them even l'chatchila to cool them — requires study; and the same for copper-kettle water this cooling helps according to all — so Ateret Zekenim; see s.k. 13. But after baking it is certainly permitted to scrape matzot faces with salt water and return to the oven as on Chol HaMoed; specifically on Chol HaMoed permitted to scrape, but on the first two nights forbidden (Ateret Zekenim).
chok-yaakov/5:_: One should forbid. That is in eating; but in benefit certainly permitted, for Mishna Berurah compared it to kneading in hot water. If he put a little salt, if baked immediately permitted in eating — end quote; and all this if kneaded with water; but if kneaded with fruit juice, Bach ruled one should not forbid b'dieved.
chok-yaakov/6:א: Valid. Nevertheless one does not fulfill the obligation of matzah with it and one does not eat it on the first night as rich matzah, since according to many poskim one fulfills with it — see above siman 462 and 471.
chok-yaakov/6:ב: And pepper. Magen Avraham wrote even one grain forbids; specifically when kneaded into it; but if it fell on it one removes it and it is permitted; ginger is treated like pepper; possibly the same for anise and saffron — end quote; the rabbi's brother-in-law in Shaarei Zedek ruled to permit in eating all kinds of spices; and so appears to me primary, for poskim mentioned only pepper; and they say: good is sharp pepper — Aruch explains because it is sharper than all spices; if so one should not compare other spices; and even in pepper one forbids only in eating like salt, as s.k. 18; and so Bach and Ateret Zekenim — they are equal.
peri-megadim/1:א: No Taz; he raised: whoever has doubt afterward, etc.; Magen Avraham 1 agreed with Beit Yosef's explanation; Darkei Moshe in Beit Yosef's explanation in Beit Yosef: all drawn at night, even at beginning of night, immediately forbidden with no remedy — somewhat so in Tur. One who wants to satisfy all views should draw at bein ha shemashot itself.
peri-megadim/1:ב: Behold Rashi Pesachim 42a s.v. shelanu explained: in Nissan, rainy season, sun travels in lower sky and springs boil — therefore we leave overnight — end quote; the reason is explained: by day sun's heat strikes them because sun travels in lower sky near water and requires cooling — mayim shelanu, measure of average night (in Nissan day and night equal). He did not explain if drawn middle of night — perhaps permitted after six hours from detachment; all wrote for Rashi whether day or night we require 12 hours detached — whence? There is also another reason: perhaps at night sun travels under ground — not mentioned in Rashi; perhaps springs do not cool until detached 12 hours — see Levush and Rosh for Rashi leniency in river water more — I did not understand per Rashi in Gemara no distinction well and cistern; other explanation sun under ground at night — leniency in river water far from source cools in ground and attached source — Magen Avraham 6 unlike Rashi; therefore must say Rashi in responsum explained like R' Eliezer of Metz — also what Rosh wrote in Nissan sun does not travel in water — see Pesachim 94b; question what Rashi wrote in Nissan days sun travels in lower sky when 94b explains in Nissan, etc. For concern sun under ground at night as sages of nations hold Pesachim 94b — some poskim hold no remedy for all drawn at night that heated, etc.; Netziv note 1 questioned: if so no water fit for kneading, for yesterday attached in ground at night heated, etc.; one can say all that were 12 hours in ground by day cooled as Magen Avraham 1; also say drawn at night at moment of movement heats — no question from yesterday attached at night — see Magen Avraham 1; and some explain further; dispute sages of Israel and nations explained Pesachim 94b: for sages of Israel sunset is sun begins setting in sky thickness, measure of travel through sky thickness is hour minus quarter of hour — 58 and a half minutes; after this measure bein ha shemashot begins — 13 and a half minutes; total hour and fifth as explained Minchat Kohen Maamar Sheini ch. 2 32a; for sages of nations sunset is beginning to set under horizon, travel through earth thickness is sunset, then bein ha shemashot as above; Taz wrote under sky — typo, should be under ground as sages of nations and Beit Yosef; see Levush 61 wrote 11 springs always boil — for Rashi as we wrote. One afraid to satisfy all views should draw precisely at bein ha shemashot — time 13 and a half minutes after hour minus quarter from sunset beginning; knead after morning light only if full 12 hours detached passed — otherwise in leap year when night sometimes not long, forbidden until full 12 hours per Rashi; if night longer than 12 hours, forbidden before day per R' Yehuda bar Natan as said — Bach; see note 2 and Magen Avraham explained further.
peri-megadim/2:_: L'chatchila Taz; Magen Avraham notes 6 and 11 — Rashi Pesachim 42a explained in Nissan rainy season — great question, for 94b explains opposite — see note 1 here; main distinction between rivers: since far from source already cooled, unlike spring where sun travels at night, etc. — see there; so Magen Avraham explains further.
peri-megadim/3:_: There is no cliche at night, and no water is permitted to be shed before the mountain, which belongs to a forbidden and unloaded fire. In Genesis Z, Magda means that if he has other water, he must pour out and see if his heart is circulated if he has other water:
peri-megadim/4:_: Iron — Taz. Salt helps for tekufah — see Yoreh De'ah 116 end ch. 5 Ra'ah Chadash. In mayim shelanu forbidden to put our salt in them — fruit juice with water hastens to become chametz siman 462, 472 in Magen Avraham 7; explained there. Forbidden for gentile to draw for matzah of mitzvah — Peri Chadash: reason like preparing for mitzvah siman 462; b'dieved permitted; when drawing say for matzah of mitzvah — Kaf HaChayim notes 8, 9. And see Eliyah Rabbah in Magen Avraham note 16 from this. Iron or seal with cloth — implies sealing with cloth cannot harm as we find all engraved and sealed, etc. — see gloss 24 months; wooden vessel no concern — explained Magen Avraham note 10; Levush seif 7 requires study.
peri-megadim/5:_: Cistern Taz wrote meaning close to drawing; so Levush — apparently when lenient in pressure it is drawn close to bein ha shemashot; for Mechaber seif 1 while still day and did not stand 12 hours, then lenient in pressure — for R' Eliezer of Metz when drawn at bein ha shemashot permitted immediately, unlike drawing beginning of night per R' Eliezer of Metz no remedy forever per second explanation in Beit Yosef — therefore do not rely on this even in cistern in pressure; nevertheless in pressure all permit. Ateret Zekenim 11; Eliyah Rabbah 6: cistern or pipe called ra'er or hole at source — perhaps ra'er water nullified with cistern water — Magen Avraham 15; see Magen Avraham 11. Those wells with ra'er in houses where they brew beer and honey and put always dirty honey-beer vessels in well — prevent drawing from well, for honey is fruit juice; some say not nullified in 1000 — siman 462; Tur prefers drawing from pipe ra'er to put vessel there and drip there.
peri-megadim/6:א: Even Taz: first night if only water not left overnight, may l'chatchila knead to fulfill eating matzah mitzvah; appears same second night although moon fixes differently, both days one law — requires study perhaps not; although obligated to eat bread — Magen Avraham 488:9 whether Torah or rabbinic — see there.
peri-megadim/6:ב: Beit Yosef wrote Taz needs explanation. Mordechai chapter Kol Sha'ah 493: incident Pesach Sunday, tekufah also fell night before; nevertheless not concerned, kneaded with water drawn at night; R' Yehuda HaChasid wrote no need to be concerned "keeper of mitzvah"; all baked only for next day, for Yom Tov does not prepare for fellow; second night too only for that day, not preparing for weekday. Per this text: nevertheless not concerned for tekufah fallen Motzei Shabbos night, drew at bein ha shemashot Motzei Shabbos as mayim shelanu and thought no prohibition in drawing, did not discard water, kneaded for day 1; likewise second night; they also hold when Pesach Sunday bake Pesach night lest matzah become stale — siman 458 Taz 1; R' Yehuda HaChasid not arguing but said they did well not discarding — keeper of mitzvah; this is Beit Yosef's language; simple they mean as those who say bake Pesach night itself — if bake Motzei Shabbos after chatzot not relevant; even per bake Pesach night wonder why not draw Friday; perhaps hold such not mayim shelanu; still wonder though tekufah fell Thursday night how permitted draw Shabbos for Yom Tov; you will say drawing not great exertion permitted; if so when tekufah fell Thursday night why concerned; they should draw Friday bein ha shemashot; further wonder tekufah: once three hours passed not tekufah hour; we concern only drinking at tekufah hour; perhaps all detached at tekufah harms afterward — end quote. Words hard to fit if text Thursday night; if text night before (mistakenly moved hei from b-lail) or explain Beit Yosef: tekufah fell Motzei Shabbos night because Pesach Sunday — "night before" means Motzei Shabbos; drew Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot with sunset as Beit Yosef beginning per R' Eliezer of Metz; simple for those who bake Pesach night — if not bake Motzei Shabbos after chatzot, already drew Thursday night belonging to Friday and baked, etc.; they also hold R' Eliezer of Metz if drawn close to sunset permitted immediately, not 12 hours unlike Rashi; R' Yehuda HaChasid said well done not discarding — keeper of mitzvah; Beit Yosef asked why not draw Friday day instead bein ha shemashot Motzei Shabbos; answer perhaps hold all drawn by day no remedy with 12 hours waiting (still wonder better Thursday night bein ha shemashot than Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot); further asked should draw Friday bein ha shemashot lighter and not Motzei Shabbos where prohibition fixed — see Magen Avraham in Mishna Berurah shevut permitted bein ha shemashot if specifically Erev Shabbos not Motzei — see there; therefore text should be tekufah fell and delete she-lamed; heaven forbid I emend and delete she-lamed.
peri-megadim/6:ג: Bach's words require study — he too explains Beit Yosef had text tekufa night before — Motzei Shabbos as here; however what he wrote there they needed water for second Pesach night — although Yom Tov does not prepare for fellow, they should also for Yom Tov 1 — some imply they drew and waited 12 hours; then night 1 Pesach whence water; therefore drew Thursday night bein ha shemashot belonging to Friday; further per conclusion all detached harms water for day 1 — should explain drew for day 1 after Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot immediately at night beginning before springs boil per R' Eliezer of Metz and knead immediately as Tur there. Bach asked why discuss tekufah fell Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot nevertheless not concerned, drew immediately after sunset and kneaded immediately per R' Eliezer of Metz — if tekufah not fallen they would draw Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot as mayim shelanu l'chatchila precisely; R' Yehuda HaChasid disagrees said not well — should draw Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot keeper of mitzvah; Bach asked since tekufah fell they draw Motzei Shabbos bein ha shemashot now too; answer all detached harms — therefore waited after tekufah passed. Taz not satisfied with many difficulties as written; therefore other explanation; Mordechai text Thursday night; Rokeach Thursday night belonging to Friday; doubtful same — sometimes call Thursday night night of 5 belonging to 6 as Rama Thursday night Magen Avraham 4; what Shabbos 9 implies apparently baked Motzei Shabbos after chatzot as siman 461; tekufah Thursday night belonging to Friday; not concerned water detached at tekufah, no iron; R' Yehuda HaChasid said well done — concludes Mordechai incident; all baked only for night 1 — Motzei Shabbos not Motzei; Pesach Sunday; Shabbos 9 proof.
peri-megadim/6:ד: Taz explained Mordechai text tekufah night before means Thursday night; "before" literally for Bach meant Sunday; reconcile Rokeach second night belonging to Thursday; they doubted because tekufah after bein ha shemashot how draw at tekufah hour — danger; nevertheless not concerned, kneaded with water drawn at night — drew immediately after tekufah; R' Yehuda HaChasid said well done; Beit Yosef challenged: still hard how depends on tekufah — without tekufah how permitted draw Thursday night for Yom Tov; answer drawing not great exertion permitted only because tekufah Thursday night they doubted and not concerned tekufah; we are Thursday night — should draw Friday bein ha shemashot better precisely l'chatchila and not violate tekufah preparation; final answer only on last question, etc. Know "kneaded with water drawn at night" — word "at night" separates "drawn" — meaning drawn at bein ha shemashot as law kneaded Pesach night. Taz Mordechai text Pesach Sunday tekufah night before — night before Pesach whether Thursday or Friday; Rokeach explains Thursday night 6 — only difference drew as law Thursday night as gloss seif 1 and baked Pesach night — they hold so siman 458; although water detached not concerned, baked, R' Yehuda HaChasid said well; all difficulties from Beit Yosef Shabbos how drew, etc.; but difficulty detached harms — Thursday night certainly no drawing as Rokeach like filling garden siman 338 (typo should be night before and Shabbos no draw); if tekufah relevance — Pesach other days detached knead Motzei after chatzot; rather "also" teaches Taz if drew Thursday night after tekufah one matter — two laws as said. Nevertheless Friday night bein ha shemashot shevut bein ha shemashot place of mitzvah Magen Avraham 4 only Shabbos no draw; Eliyah Rabbah 17 agrees Taz; drawn Thursday night means bein ha shemashot; some erred baked by day meaning Motzei because mitzvah beloved in its time proper Motzei.
